proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(L:=\log(en)\), and apply
\(\mathtt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_heterogeneity\_frontier}/\mathtt{thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution}\)
to the outcome \(\widetilde Y:=Y/2\).  This application is legitimate for every
\(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\).  Indeed,
\[
 |E_P[\widetilde Y\mid A=a,X=k]|=|\mu_{ak}|/2\le M/2
\]
by \(ass:cell\text{-}mean\text{-}envelope\), and Lyapunov's elementary moment
inequality, proved here by Cauchy--Schwarz, gives
\[
 E_P[(\widetilde Y-\mu_{ak}/2)^2\mid A=a,X=k]
 \le \{E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^4\mid A=a,X=k]\}^{1/2}/4
 \le M^2/4.
\tag{1}
\]
The source model's heterogeneity parameter can be set to \(2\), since the
scaled conditional effects and their average both lie in \([-M,M]\).  Fixed
overlap is exactly \(ass:fixed\text{-}overlap\), and the sample split remains
independent by \(ass:iid\text{-}sampling\).

We spell out the algebra that turns the imported one-mark lift into the four
coordinates in the present core.  Write
\[
 x_0=p_k(1-\pi_k),\qquad x_1=p_k\pi_k,\qquad
 z_a=x_a\mu_{ak},\qquad p_k=x_0+x_1.
\tag{2}
\]
The calibrated source construction takes
\[
 K=\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor,\quad
 \alpha_0=\min\{1,(64\log6)^{-1},(512D_6)^{-1}\},
 \quad D_6=8\log(27/4),
\]
and \(B=4096L/m_1\), where \(m_1\) is the size of its estimation fold; its
pilot threshold is \(256L\).  Select \(c_L=\alpha_0\).  Then \(K\le L_n\),
and all source polynomials belong to the larger space \(\mathscr Q_{L_n}\).
For the shifted Chebyshev polynomial \(T_K\), define, with continuous values at
zero,
\[
 H_K(t)=\frac{1-T_K(1-2t)}{2K^2},\qquad
 E_K(t)=\frac{H_K(t)}t,\qquad
 G_K(t)=\frac{1-E_K(t)}t.
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(T_K(\cos\vartheta)=\cos(K\vartheta)\),
\[
 0\le t\{1-tG_K(t)\}=H_K(t)\le K^{-2},
 \qquad 0\le t\le1.
\tag{4}
\]
Moreover \(G_K\) has degree at most \(K-2\).  Consequently
\[
 q_a(x_0,x_1):=\frac{x_0+x_1}{B}G_K(x_a/B)
\]
has degree at most \(K-1\le L_n-1\), and
\[
 (x_0,z_0,x_1,z_1)\longmapsto z_1q_1(x_0,x_1)-z_0q_0(x_0,x_1)
 \in\mathscr Q_{L_n}.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus (5) is precisely the four-coordinate representation claimed in
\(def:four\text{-}coordinate\text{-}lift\text{-}handle\).

For completeness, consider any selected light cell on the pilot-good event,
so that \(p_k\le B/4\).  By overlap, \(x_a\ge\epsilon p_k\).  Equations
(2)--(4), \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M\), and \(x_a/B\in[0,1]\) imply
\[
 \left|p_k\mu_{ak}-\frac{p_kz_a}{B}G_K(x_a/B)\right|
 =p_k|\mu_{ak}|\frac{H_K(x_a/B)}{x_a/B}
 \le \frac{MB}{\epsilon K^2}.
\tag{6}
\]
The ordered distinct-index falling-factorial statistic carrying one outcome
mark is unbiased for every monomial \(z_ap_kx_a^j\): expanding its expectation
as a sum over distinct indices and using independence gives the product of the
corresponding one-observation expectations.  Hence linearity and (6), first
conditionally on the pilot and then unconditionally, yield
\[
 \left|E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
 \widehat T_{\mathrm L}-
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})
 \right]\right|
 \le \frac{2MdB}{\epsilon K^2}+\mathcal E_{\mathrm{pilot}}.
\tag{7}
\]
The binomial Chernoff calculation contained in the imported construction gives
for its pilot-good event \(\mathcal A\))
\[
 Q_P^{(n)}(\mathcal A^c)\le 2d\exp(-c\,256L)\le Cn^{-6}
\tag{8}
\]
after reducing \(c_\epsilon\) if necessary.  The same construction's explicit
coefficient bound \(6^{2K}\le n^{1/32}\), together with its factorial second
moment identity and (1), gives by Cauchy--Schwarz
\(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{pilot}}\le C_\epsilon Mn^{-2}\).  This is at most
\(C_\epsilon Md/(nL)\) after enlarging the constant over the finitely many
small values of \(n\).  Since \(m_1\asymp n\), \(B\asymp L/n\), and
\(K\asymp L\), (7) becomes
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}
 \left|E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
 \widehat T_{\mathrm L}-
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})
 \right]\right|
 \le C_\epsilon M\frac{d}{n\log(en)}.
\tag{9}
\]
Equation (8) proves the asserted pilot-misclassification order as well.
Finally, the coefficient recurrence has \(O(L_n^2)\) coefficients, and the
four-coordinate bookkeeping and pilot split add at most a factor \(L_n\), so
the imported \(O(dL_n^2)\) implementation is, in particular,
\(O(dL_n^3)\).  Rescaling the marks by one half and multiplying the output by
two preserves every expectation identity, zero fallback, and clipping rule.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}\).  From
\(ass:control\text{-}arm\text{-}zero\text{-}subclass\) and consistency,
\(Y=0\) almost surely on \(\{A=0\}\).  Therefore, on every positive-mass
cell, \(\mu_{0k}=E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=k]=0\); the conditioning event has positive
probability because \(ass:fixed\text{-}overlap\) gives
\(P(A=0,X=k)=p_k(1-\pi_k)\ge\epsilon p_k>0\).  The identifying equality in
\(def:ate\text{-}functional\) now gives
\[
 \tau(P)=\sum_{k=1}^dp_k\mu_{1k}=\psi_1(P).
\tag{1}
\]

To verify the scaling rather than merely relabel the estimand, start with a
binary treated outcome \(B\in\{0,1\}\) in the hard family of
\(lem:zeng\text{-}one\text{-}arm\text{-}lower\), put \(Y(0)=0\), and put
\(Y(1)=MB\).  Leave \(X\), the cell masses, and the propensities unchanged,
and generate treatment conditionally independently of the potential outcomes
given \(X\).  This gives conditional exchangeability; defining
\(Y=Y(A)\) gives consistency.  Its cell means satisfy
\(0\le\mu_{1k}\le M\) and \(\mu_{0k}=0\).  Furthermore
\[
 |Y(1)-E[Y(1)\mid X=k]|\le M,
 \qquad Y(0)-E[Y(0)\mid X=k]=0,
\]
so every required conditional fourth central moment is at most \(M^4\).
Thus every scaled law lies in
\(\mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}\subseteq
\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\).  Both sides of (1) are multiplied by \(M\),
and squared error is multiplied by \(M^2\).  The cited one-arm lower bound
therefore gives, by restricting the supremum from
\(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\) to this subclass,
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(\widehat\tau-\tau(P))^2]
 \ge c_\epsilon M^2\left\{n^{-1}+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}
\]
throughout the source theorem's stated range.  This is a point-estimation
conclusion only.  Nothing in this reduction itself supplies two concentrated,
ATE-separated priors or controls their prior-predictive total variation, which
explains the final qualification in the proposition.

Let
\[
 A_j:=\{C_n\cap\mathcal T_j\ne\varnothing\},\qquad j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Uniform coverage and the support condition in
\(def:prior\text{-}predictive\text{-}pair\) imply
\[
 \mathbb Q_j(A_j)
 \ge\int Q_P^{(n)}\{\tau(P)\in C_n\}\,d\Pi_j(P)
 \ge1-\alpha.
\tag{1}
\]
By the defining variational inequality for total variation,
\[
 \mathbb Q_0(A_1)\ge \mathbb Q_1(A_1)
 -\|\mathbb Q_0-\mathbb Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \ge1-\alpha-\|\mathbb Q_0-\mathbb Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\tag{2}
\]
The union bound applied under \(\mathbb Q_0\) to (1)--(2) gives
\[
 \mathbb Q_0(A_0\cap A_1)
 \ge1-2\alpha-\|\mathbb Q_0-\mathbb Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\tag{3}
\]
On \(A_0\cap A_1\), the interval \(C_n\) contains a point of each target
set.  Because it is an interval, its length is at least
\(\Delta(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1)\).  Multiplying this deterministic
inequality by \(\mathbf1_{A_0\cap A_1}\), taking \(\mathbb Q_0\)-expectations,
and replacing the right side of (3) by its positive part proves the claim.

By \(thm:global\text{-}honest\text{-}upper\), the particular measurable
interval \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}\) is admissible in the infimum defining
\(\mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}
 \le \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[|\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}|]
 \le C_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}.
\tag{1}
\]
Conversely, \(thm:same\text{-}class\text{-}testing\text{-}converse\) applies
to every interval admitted by \(def:minimax\text{-}honest\text{-}length\), so
taking first its supremum over \(P\) and then the infimum over intervals gives
\[
 \mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}
 \ge c_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}.
\tag{2}
\]
Substitution of \(def:frontier\text{-}scale\) into (1)--(2) proves the displayed
equivalence uniformly on \(d\le c_\epsilon n\log(en)\).  Finally,
\(prop:certified\text{-}finite\text{-}precision\text{-}implementation\) gives
coverage of the outward-rounded interval and adds at most
\(2\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\le2r_{n,d,M}\) to its expected length.  Thus it has
the same constant-order upper bound.

Use the corrected construction of \(\widehat C^{\mathrm G}\), which intersects
the Gaussian interval with \([-2M,2M]\).  Write
\[
 r_{\mathrm G}:=z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/n},
 \qquad r_{\mathrm H}:=\widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}}.
\]
The two ratio-consistency conclusions of \(thm:local\text{-}linearization\),
together with
\(v_0M^2\le V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\le v_1M^2\), imply
\[
 \sqrt{\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}}
 -\sqrt{\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}}=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(1).
\tag{1}
\]
Indeed, after division by \(\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)}\), each square root
converges in probability to one, while the variance band makes the multiplying
factor bounded.  The radius expansion in the same theorem and (1) give
\[
 r_{\mathrm H}-r_{\mathrm G}
 =o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{2}
\]
Its center expansion gives
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}
 =o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{3}
\]
Consequently each corresponding unprojected endpoint differs by at most the
sum of the absolute values in (2)--(3), hence by
\(o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2})\).  The maps
\(x\mapsto\max\{-2M,x\}\) and \(x\mapsto\min\{2M,x\}\) are
one-Lipschitz.  Applying them to the lower and upper endpoints proves the first
displayed assertion, including laws for which \(\tau(P_n)\) is on the boundary.

For a valid finite-precision input,
\(prop:certified\text{-}finite\text{-}precision\text{-}implementation\) moves
each robust endpoint outward by at most \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\).  If
\(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}=o(n^{-1/2})\), the triangle inequality therefore gives
the same endpoint conclusion.  Finally, finite-sample honesty of the exact-real
and outward-rounded robust intervals follows respectively from
\(thm:global\text{-}honest\text{-}upper\) and
\(prop:certified\text{-}finite\text{-}precision\text{-}implementation\).  This
last argument uses no Gaussian approximation on the unrestricted global class.

If \(d_n=d\) is fixed, then \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), so the dimension condition is
automatic.  Membership in
\(\mathcal B_{\epsilon,M,c_0,v_0,v_1}\) retains, by definition, the lower cell
mass bound \(P_n(X=k)\ge c_0/d\) and the variance band
\(v_0M^2\le V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\le v_1M^2\).  Substituting fixed \(d\) into
\(thm:local\text{-}linearization\) gives the efficient-influence-function
expansion, its standardized normal limit, and ratio consistency of both stated
variance estimators.  Substituting the same facts into
\(thm:endpoint\text{-}equivalence\) identifies the first-order endpoints with
those of the saturated-cell Wald interval.  These are exactly the three
conclusions asserted in the proposition.

added_lemmas.statement: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2, establishes on its unit-scale binary one-arm model the minimax squared-error lower bound \(\gtrsim_{\epsilon}\{n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\}\) for estimating \(\psi_1(P)\) in the dimension range used in Appendix C.5.

attestation.note: The immutable local bibliography supplies the stable arXiv handle and identifies the exact theorem and appendix; no verbatim theorem transcription is present in the supplied snapshot.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(n,d\ge1\), there are two point-mass priors
\(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) supported on \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\) and singleton
target sets \(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1\) such that
\[
 \Delta(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1)\ge
 2\min\left\{\frac14,
 \sqrt{\frac{3\log\{1+(1-2\alpha)^2\}}{32}}\right\}Mn^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \|\mathbb Q_0-\mathbb Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le(1-2\alpha)/2,
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(t:=1-2\alpha\in(1/2,1)\),
\[
 h_n:=\min\left\{\frac14,
 \sqrt{\frac{3\log(1+t^2)}{32n}}\right\},
 \qquad q_j:=\frac12+(2j-1)h_n.
\tag{1}
\]
For \(j\in\{0,1\}\), construct \(P_j\) as follows.  Set \(X=1\) almost
surely, let \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), let
\(B_j\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_j)\) independently of \(A\), and set
\(Y(0)=0\), \(Y(1)=MB_j\), and \(Y=Y(A)\).  Cells \(k>1\) have zero mass.
Consistency and conditional exchangeability hold by construction, overlap
holds because \(\pi_1=1/2\), the cell means lie in \([0,M]\), and
\(|Y(a)-E[Y(a)\mid X=1]|\le M\).  Hence \(P_j\in
\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\).  Moreover
\[
 \tau(P_j)=Mq_j,\qquad |\tau(P_1)-\tau(P_0)|=2Mh_n.
\tag{2}
\]

Let \(R_j\) be the one-observation observed law.  The only probabilities that
differ are those of \((A,Y)=(1,M)\) and \((1,0)\).  Direct summation of the
Pearson divergence gives
\[
 \chi^2(R_0,R_1)
 =2h_n^2\left(\frac1{q_1}+\frac1{1-q_1}\right)
 =\frac{2h_n^2}{q_1(1-q_1)}
 \le\frac{32}{3}h_n^2,
\tag{3}
\]
because \(q_1\in[1/2,3/4]\).  If \(L=dR_0/dR_1\), independence and
Fubini's theorem yield the exact product identity
\[
 1+\chi^2(R_0^{\otimes n},R_1^{\otimes n})
 =E_{R_1^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\prod_{i=1}^nL(O_i)^2\right]
 =\{1+\chi^2(R_0,R_1)\}^n.
\tag{4}
\]
Also, Cauchy--Schwarz gives directly
\[
 \|R_0^{\otimes n}-R_1^{\otimes n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =\frac12E_{R_1^{\otimes n}}|L_n-1|
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(R_0^{\otimes n},R_1^{\otimes n})}.
\tag{5}
\]
Equations (1), (3)--(5), and \(1+x\le e^x\) imply the desired bound
\(t/2\).  In the case where the minimum in (1) equals \(1/4\), the same
calculation applies because that case entails
\(\exp(2/3)-1\le t^2\).  Finally, with
\[
 c_\alpha:=2\min\left\{\frac14,
 \sqrt{\frac{3\log(1+t^2)}{32}}\right\}>0,
\]
equations (1)--(2) give \(2Mh_n\ge c_\alpha Mn^{-1/2}\).  Taking
\(\Pi_j\) to be the point mass at \(P_j\) and
\(\mathcal T_j=\{\tau(P_j)\}\) completes the construction.

proposed_definition_changes.reason: The robust interval is intersected with the known parameter range \([-2M,2M]\), but the frozen Gaussian comparator is not. An explicit witness is \(d=1\), \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), \(Y(1)=M+Z\), and \(Y(0)=-M+Z\), where \(Z\) is an independent symmetric \(\{ -\sigma,\sigma\}\)-valued variable with \(0<\sigma\le M\). Then \(\tau(P)=2M\) and \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=4\sigma^2\); whenever this variance lies in the declared band, the unprojected Gaussian upper endpoint has a nonvanishing root-\(n\) excess over \(2M\), whereas the robust upper endpoint is at most \(2M\). Intersecting the comparator with the same range is the minimal formula correction, and projection is one-Lipschitz.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The corrected construction uses \(M\), so both the formula and the complete definition metadata must be replaced atomically.

proposed.statement:
Apply CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026,
\(thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution\), to the marks
\(Y/2\) and multiply its clipped output by two.  For
\(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), the resulting banked real-mark heavy-light
estimator admits the four-coordinate representation in
\(def:four\text{-}coordinate\text{-}lift\text{-}handle\), is computable using
\(O(dL_n^3)\) arithmetic operations, and satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}
 \left|E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
 \widehat T_{\mathrm L}-
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})
 \right]\right|
 \lesssim_{\epsilon}\frac{Md}{n\log(en)};
\]
its pilot misclassification contribution has the same order.  The
representation preserves the banked factorial coefficients, zero fallbacks,
clipping, and expectation identities and exposes the selected marked-factorial
statistic required by \(def:direct\text{-}calibration\text{-}handle\).
proposed.justification: This compatibility lemma imports the established real-mark heavy-light approximation and verifies exactly the representation needed by the new observable tail score; it is not an independent approximation novelty claim.
proposed.gap: The accepted external construction supplies the clipped real-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator and its risk order. The proof here exposes its pilot-selected light statistic in a form on which data-only calibration could act without changing its expectation and bias guarantees.
proposed.consumer: The bias half of the globally honest upper interval and the rare-cell contribution in the \(n=9915,d=8196\) 401(k) analysis.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The frozen statement explicitly invokes a theorem from another CausalSmith run, so its required cross-run provenance must be recorded.

proposed.statement:
On \(\mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}\),
\(\tau(P)=\psi_1(P)\) because \(\mu_{0k}=0\) on every positive-mass cell.
More explicitly, take the control-arm-zero binary hard family used in
ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, leave its zero
control outcome fixed, and multiply its binary treated outcome by \(M\).  The
induced full-data laws belong to
\(\mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}\subseteq
\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\), preserve cell masses and propensities, satisfy the
fourth-central-moment envelope, and multiply both \(\psi_1\)-separation and ATE
separation by \(M\).  Consequently the theorem's one-arm mean-squared-error
lower scale \(M^2\{n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\}\) transfers by subclass
restriction to ATE point estimation for
\(d\lesssim_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\).  Its priors may be used in
\(thm:same\text{-}class\text{-}testing\text{-}converse\) only after that theorem
separately proves ATE target-set separation and prior-predictive total-variation
control.
proposed.justification: The source result concerns the treated-arm functional, so an explicit control-zero embedding is required before its rate can inform any ATE lower-bound argument.
proposed.gap: The cited theorem lower-bounds \(\psi_1\) and uses a control-arm-zero proof family; the proposition records the exact subclass and scaling identity that transfer that source experiment to the ATE model without relabeling the published estimand.
proposed.consumer: The rare-cell source priors for the direct same-class confidence-length converse.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The published one-arm minimax lower bound is a logical premise and therefore must be a cited leaf in the dependency graph.

proposed.statement:
For every \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), there exist priors
\(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) supported on the same class
\(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\) and sets
\(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1\) such that
\(\Delta(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1)\gtrsim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\) and
\(\|\mathbb Q_0-\mathbb Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le(1-2\alpha)/2\).  The rare-cell
component starts from the control-arm-zero embedding in
\(prop:zeng\text{-}one\text{-}arm\text{-}to\text{-}ate\text{-}reduction\), then
constructs ATE-separated prior supports and verifies prior-predictive
total-variation control directly; separate root-\(n\) and saturation priors
complete the range.  The resulting confidence-length bound
\(\mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\gtrsim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\)
follows through \(lem:coverage\text{-}testing\text{-}inequality\), not by taking
the square root of the published mean-squared-error bound.
proposed.justification: This certifies the full confidence-width lower frontier in the identical raw conditional fourth-central-moment class used by the interval.
proposed.gap: The published point-risk theorem does not itself place separated ATE sets inside two same-class priors or invoke uniform coverage to lower-bound expected interval length.
proposed.consumer: The minimax optimality certificate for the robust interval and a diagnostic showing why shorter 401(k) intervals cannot be uniformly honest without added structure.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The explicit same-class root-\(n\) testing construction is a load-bearing part of the claimed converse and must be wired into it.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Constructing the requested measurable rare-cell radius with a direct finite-sample tail certificate, sharp expected radius, explicit bounded-influence perturbation score, and certified numerical inversion.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen handles do not define the selected statistic or the perturbation score as maps from the sample: they give no block sizes, factorial coefficients after selection, bounded-influence function, variance proxy, or inversion equation. Consequently measurability, the exponential-score inequality, and the expected radius cannot be calculated. Treating the prose instruction as if it already supplied those properties would assume the crux.
open_obligations.attempted: I transplanted the banked Chebyshev constants and derived the light-branch bias, then considered independent block estimates and a Catoni score. A block estimate with degree \(L_n\asymp\log n\) does not automatically retain the full-sample factorial variance after subdivision, and centering a robust block aggregate does not yield a tail bound for the frozen full-sample statistic without an explicit coupling. The forbidden MSE-to-Chebyshev conversion would bypass precisely this missing step.
open_obligations.partial_result: The four-coordinate representation and its bias order are proved in \(lem:four\text{-}coordinate\text{-}bias\); no tail premise was inferred from that bias calculation.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The finite-sample coverage and expected-radius analysis for the complete heavy-light interval.
open_obligations.obstruction: The rare radius is unresolved, and the heavy branch is likewise only a prose handle: no truncation threshold, self-normalized score, allocation of the noncoverage budget, or formula for the total radius is declared. The bias lemma alone cannot imply honesty.
open_obligations.attempted: I decomposed the target error into pilot, light-bias, light-fluctuation, and heavy-fluctuation terms. The light bias closes, but neither fluctuation event is attached to a defined observable radius.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved four-coordinate lemma supplies the deterministic rare-cell bias
order \(Md/[n\log(en)]\).  If one had an explicit data-only rare radius with
the two guarantees posed in \(oeq:observable\text{-}rare\text{-}tail\), plus an
explicit heavy-branch score with its allocated coverage probability and
expected radius \(O_{\epsilon,\alpha}(Mn^{-1/2})\), then a union bound over the
two branches and the triangle inequality would give the stated global coverage
and expected-length order.  Those tail premises are not consequences of the
current construction handles.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A forward-error bound and bit-complexity proof for the actual score and factorial-polynomial evaluation.
open_obligations.obstruction: Because the score, coefficient array, perturbation blocks, and critical-value equation are not defined, there is no expression whose Lipschitz or coefficient-growth bound can justify the stated working precision. The construction text asserts outward arithmetic but does not prove that the accumulated error is at most the requested endpoint tolerance.
open_obligations.attempted: I verified the deterministic consequences of a certified endpoint enclosure, but the missing real-arithmetic error bound cannot be reconstructed from the input-length formula alone.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Conditional on a certified arithmetic analysis proving that each computed
endpoint lies outward from its exact-real counterpart by a quantity in
\([0,\delta_{\mathrm{num}}]\), interval inclusion is immediate, coverage is
monotone under inclusion, and the length increases by at most
\(2\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\).  The missing part is the antecedent: no formula or
coefficient-growth bound for the score being evaluated is present in the core.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The rare-cell same-class testing priors with both concentrated ATE separation of order \(Md/[n\log(en)]\) and prior-predictive total-variation control.
open_obligations.obstruction: The cited source supplies a squared-error lower bound for the one-arm functional, not the two target-set concentration and mixture-closeness statements required by the confidence-length inequality. Those properties do not follow logically by taking a square root of risk.
open_obligations.attempted: I constructed and proved the direct same-class root-\(n\) two-point experiment and proved the general coverage-to-length inequality. The local snapshot contains no explicit rare-cell testing priors or moment-matching certificate from which the missing total-variation calculation can be reproduced.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved testing inequality and \(lem:root\text{-}n\text{-}testing\text{-}priors\)
give directly
\[
 \mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\ge c_\alpha Mn^{-1/2}
\]
on the same class.  The remaining rare-cell term requires two prior supports
whose ATE values concentrate in separated sets at distance
\(Md/[n\log(en)]\) while their prior-predictive laws have the required total
variation bound; a squared-error minimax lower bound alone does not imply
these two properties.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The first-order equivalence, ratio-consistent variance, and Gaussian-radius expansion for the heavy-light outputs.
open_obligations.obstruction: The saturated one-step comparator is explicit and its nuisance rates follow from balanced cells, but the heavy-light estimator, variance output, and radius are not explicit maps. Nothing in the frozen handles states that the rare branch switches off, that the heavy branch equals the one-step score to first order, or that its direct critical value converges to the Gaussian quantile.
open_obligations.attempted: I derived the saturated-cell nuisance rates, orthogonal remainder, empirical-process remainder, variance consistency, and Lyapunov condition. The same comparison cannot be written for the unnamed heavy-light summands.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The saturated comparator part can be derived from the frozen assumptions.  If
\(g(O;\eta)\) denotes the augmented inverse-propensity score in
\(def:saturated\text{-}one\text{-}step\), then for every training fold,
binomial reciprocal-count identities and the conditional second-moment bound
implied by \(ass:conditional\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment\) give
\[
 \sum_kp_k(\widehat\mu_{ak}-\mu_{ak})^2=O_P(d_n/n),
 \qquad
 \sum_kp_k(\widehat\pi_k-\pi_k)^2=O_P(d_n/n).
\]
Conditional expectation of the score difference equals
\[
 \sum_kp_k(\widehat\pi_k-\pi_k)
 \left\{\frac{\widehat\mu_{1k}-\mu_{1k}}{\widehat\pi_k}
 +\frac{\widehat\mu_{0k}-\mu_{0k}}{1-\widehat\pi_k}\right\},
\]
whose absolute value is \(O_P(d_n/n)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\) by clipped overlap and
\(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\).  Conditional variance of the centered score difference is
\(O_P(d_n/n)\), so cross-fitting makes its empirical average
\(O_P(\sqrt{d_n}/n)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\).  Hence
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)
 =n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\]
The envelope and overlap assumptions give
\(E_{P_n}|\phi_{P_n}|^4\le C_\epsilon M^4\); therefore the oracle empirical
second moment converges to \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\), and the preceding
score-difference bound gives
\(\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\to1\).  The same fourth-moment
bound verifies the Lyapunov ratio, so the standardized oracle sum, and hence
the one-step estimator, is asymptotically standard normal.  What is not derived
is any corresponding assertion about the undefined heavy-light outputs.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove that, on the fixed-alphabet all-heavy event, the heavy--light point estimate differs from the saturated one-step estimate by a term negligible at the root-sample-size scale and their variance outputs differ by a term negligible relative to the squared outcome scale; also clarify or witness the claimed failure of absolute Wald endpoint equivalence.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen heavy--light handle names point and variance outputs but supplies no formulas for the heavy-cell estimator, truncation threshold, self-normalized score, aggregation weights, or variance statistic. Thus no equation connects those outputs to the explicit saturated one-step score on the all-heavy event. The zero-variance law disproves standardized-normal and variance-ratio conclusions, but does not by itself disprove an absolute endpoint comparison at the root-sample-size scale.
open_obligations.attempted: Reduced fixed-alphabet balance and overlap to uniform positive arm-cell masses; proved that empty training cells are exponentially unlikely and that pilot light-cell selection vanishes; expanded the explicit cross-fitted saturated score fold by fold; and attempted to transfer that expansion on the all-heavy event. The transfer stops exactly where the heavy--light handle omits its sample formulas, so postulating it would assume the crux.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The saturated one-step conclusions and the obstruction to studentization can be proved from the frozen primitives.  Write
\[
 p_{k,n}=P_n(X=k),\qquad
 \pi_{k,n}=P_n(A=1\mid X=k),\qquad
 \sigma_{ak,n}^2=E_{P_n}\!\left[(Y-\mu_{ak,n})^2\mid X=k,A=a\right].
\]
The conditional fourth-moment assumption and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\(\sigma_{ak,n}^2\le M^2\).  Define
\[
 h_{k,n}=\mu_{1k,n}-\mu_{0k,n}-\tau(P_n)
\]
and let \(\phi_n=\phi_{P_n}\).  Conditional centering of the two outcome residuals, mutual exclusivity of \(A\) and \(1-A\), and the definition of \(\phi_{P_n}\) yield the orthogonal variance decomposition
\[
 V_n:=V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)
 =\sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}\left\{
 h_{k,n}^2+\frac{\sigma_{1k,n}^2}{\pi_{k,n}}
 +\frac{\sigma_{0k,n}^2}{1-\pi_{k,n}}
 \right\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, the conditional mean of the residual part of \(\phi_n\) given \(X=k\) is zero, so its cross product with \(h_{k,n}\) has expectation zero; the product of its treated and control summands is identically zero.  Each term on the right-hand side of (1) is nonnegative.  Consequently,
\[
 \sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}\sigma_{ak,n}^2\le V_n,
 \qquad
 \sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}h_{k,n}^2\le V_n.
 \tag{2}
\]

We next establish the expansion for the estimator in \(\texttt{def:saturated-one-step}\).  For a validation fold \(I_s\), let \(\mathcal D_n^{(-s)}=(O_j:j\notin I_s)\) be its training sample, let \(m_{s,n}=n-|I_s|\), and put
\[
 q_{1k,n}=p_{k,n}\pi_{k,n},\qquad
 q_{0k,n}=p_{k,n}(1-\pi_{k,n}).
\]
The balance and overlap hypotheses imply
\[
 q_{ak,n}\ge q_*:=\frac{c_0\epsilon}{d}>0.
 \tag{3}
\]
Because \(K_0\) is fixed and fold sizes differ by at most one, there is a constant \(c_K>0\) such that \(m_{s,n}\ge c_Kn\) for every \(s\) and all sufficiently large \(n\).  If \(N_{ak}^{(-s)}\) denotes the number of training observations in arm-cell \((a,k)\), independence gives
\[
 \Pr\{N_{ak}^{(-s)}=0\}=(1-q_{ak,n})^{m_{s,n}}
 \le \exp(-c_Kq_*n).
 \tag{4}
\]
Thus every training arm-cell is nonempty with probability at least
\(1-2dK_0\exp(-c_Kq_*n)\).

Put
\[
 e_{ak}^{(-s)}=\widehat\mu_{ak}^{(-s)}-\mu_{ak,n},
 \qquad
 \delta_k^{(-s)}=\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}-\pi_{k,n}.
\]
For a binomial variable \(N\) with parameters \((m,q)\) and \(mq\ge1\), splitting according to \(N\ge mq/2\) and using Chebyshev's inequality on the complementary event gives
\[
 E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf 1\{N>0\}}{N}\right]
 \le \frac{2}{mq}+\Pr\{|N-mq|\ge mq/2\}
 \le \frac{6}{mq}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Conditional on \(N_{ak}^{(-s)}\), a nonempty-cell outcome mean is unbiased and has conditional variance \(\sigma_{ak,n}^2/N_{ak}^{(-s)}\); on an empty cell the zero fallback has squared error at most \(M^2\).  Equations (3)--(5) therefore imply, with constants depending only on \((d,c_0,\epsilon,K_0)\),
\[
 E\!\left[(e_{ak}^{(-s)})^2\right]
 \le \frac{C\sigma_{ak,n}^2}{n}+CM^2e^{-cn}.
 \tag{6}
\]
For the propensity estimate, condition first on the number of training observations with \(X=k\), apply the binomial variance formula, and then apply (5).  Clipping cannot increase distance from \(\pi_{k,n}\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), so
\[
 E\!\left[(\delta_k^{(-s)})^2\right]\le \frac{C}{n}+Ce^{-cn}.
 \tag{7}
\]

Define the oracle uncentered score
\[
 \psi_n(O)=\mu_{1X,n}-\mu_{0X,n}
 +\frac{A(Y-\mu_{1X,n})}{\pi_{X,n}}
 -\frac{(1-A)(Y-\mu_{0X,n})}{1-\pi_{X,n}}
 =\tau(P_n)+\phi_n(O).
 \tag{8}
\]
For \(i\in I_s\), set \(D_{i,s}=\widehat\psi_i-\psi_n(O_i)\).  Conditional on the training sample, direct substitution in the score gives
\[
 E[D_{i,s}\mid X_i=k,\mathcal D_n^{(-s)}]
 =\delta_k^{(-s)}\left\{
 \frac{e_{1k}^{(-s)}}{\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}}
 +\frac{e_{0k}^{(-s)}}{1-\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}}
 \right\}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Both denominators in (9) are at least \(\epsilon/2\).  Hence (2), (6), (7), Cauchy--Schwarz, and the fact that \(d\) is fixed show that the conditional score bias \(B_{s,n}=E[D_{i,s}\mid\mathcal D_n^{(-s)}]\) satisfies
\[
 E|B_{s,n}|
 \le C\left(\frac{\sqrt{V_n}}{n}+Me^{-cn}\right),
 \qquad
 \sqrt n B_{s,n}=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(1).
 \tag{10}
\]
The last conclusion uses only \(V_n\le C_{\epsilon}M^2\), which follows from (1), the mean envelope, the second-moment consequence of the fourth-moment assumption, and overlap.

The same substitution before taking conditional expectations, followed by \((x_1+\cdots+x_r)^2\le r\sum_jx_j^2\), gives
\[
 E[D_{i,s}^2\mid\mathcal D_n^{(-s)}]
 \le C\sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}\left[
 (e_{1k}^{(-s)})^2+(e_{0k}^{(-s)})^2
 +(\delta_k^{(-s)})^2(\sigma_{1k,n}^2+\sigma_{0k,n}^2)
 \right].
 \tag{11}
\]
Equations (2), (6), and (7) imply that the expectation of the right-hand side of (11) is at most
\(C V_n/n+CM^2e^{-cn}=o(M^2)\).  Conditional Chebyshev applied separately to the fixed number of validation folds, together with (10), now yields
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{s=0}^{K_0-1}\sum_{i\in I_s}D_{i,s}=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(1).
 \tag{12}
\]
Combining (8) and (12) proves
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_n(O_i)+o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(1).
 \tag{13}
\]
The summands in (13) are independent, centered, and have variance \(V_n\) by (1).  Therefore Chebyshev's inequality and the premise \(V_n/M^2\to0\) give
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_n(O_i)\to0
 \quad\text{in }Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\text{-probability},
\]
and hence
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)\}\to0.
 \tag{14}
\]

It remains to check the absolute variance conclusion.  The mean envelope, overlap, and conditional fourth-moment bound imply
\(E_{P_n}[\phi_n(O)^4]\le C_\epsilon M^4\).  Thus
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_n(O_i)^2-V_n\to0
 \quad\text{in }Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\text{-probability}
 \tag{15}
\]
by Chebyshev's inequality.  Moreover, (11) and Markov's inequality give
\(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,s(i)}^2=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(M^2)\), where \(s(i)\) is the fold containing \(i\).  Since centering minimizes an empirical sum of squares,
\[
 0\le\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}
 \le\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat\psi_i-\tau(P_n)\}^2
 \le\frac2n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_n(O_i)^2
 +\frac2n\sum_{i=1}^nD_{i,s(i)}^2.
 \tag{16}
\]
Equations (15)--(16) and \(V_n/M^2\to0\) prove
\[
 \widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/M^2\to0.
 \tag{17}
\]

There is also an explicit certificate showing why studentization and relative variance consistency do not follow.  Let \(P_n=P^0\) for every \(n\), where \(X\) is uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\), \(A\) is independent of \(X\) with probability \(1/2\), and \(Y(0)=Y(1)=Y=0\) almost surely.  Consistency and conditional exchangeability hold by construction; overlap holds because \(\epsilon<1/2\); the cell-mean and fourth-moment bounds hold with value zero; and \(p_k=1/d\ge c_0/d\).  The influence function is identically zero, so
\[
 V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^0)=0.
\]
Consequently both the standardized statistic with denominator
\(\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^0)}\) and the ratio
\(\widehat V/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^0)\) are undefined.  This member of the stated class rules out any uniformly quantified standardized-normal or ratio-consistency conclusion under the proposition's premises alone.

The parallel assertions for \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}\) and \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}\) cannot yet be derived.  The frozen construction \(\texttt{def:robust-heavy-light-interval-handle}\) does not specify the sample map for its heavy-cell point estimate, its truncation threshold, its self-normalized score, its aggregation weights, or its variance output.  Fixed \(d\), balance, and overlap do imply that every pilot cell exceeds any fixed numerical multiple of \(\log(en)\) with probability tending to one: for all sufficiently large \(n\), the lower-tail event is contained in a deviation of at least half the binomial mean, whose probability is \(O(n^{-1})\) by Chebyshev.  But the handle contains no algebraic identity on this all-heavy event from which one could compare its outputs with (13) and (17).  The missing load-bearing statement is
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}\}=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(1),
 \qquad
 \{\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}-\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}\}/M^2=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(1)
 \tag{18}
\]
under fixed \(d\), balance, overlap, and \(V_n/M^2\to0\).  Proving (18) requires the omitted formulas; assuming (18) would assume the crux.  The zero-variance witness above also does not by itself refute an absolute \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) endpoint comparison, so the last endpoint non-implication in the target likewise requires either a precise intended relative-Wald formulation or an explicit counterexample after the heavy--light interval is fully defined.
